_meta.usage: Maps to the ScriptableObjects in the design doc (ChapterDefinition, GeneratorDefinition, UpgradeDefinition, EventDefinition, BarDefinition, RewardDefinition). Either hand-author SOs from these values or write a small importer. ALL ScriptableObjects are discovered at runtime through Addressables (labels per type), not direct references. All numbers are starter values for tuning; the Records capstone gate is the primary pacing knob.

modelNotes.conditions: Every gate/unlock/visibility/availability rule is a single discriminated Condition shape — always an object with a `type` field — evaluated by ONE ConditionEvaluator. No bare/heterogeneous shapes. Types used in Ch1: `currency` (current balance ≥ value), `currencyEarnedTotal` (lifetime earned ≥ value), `ownedCount` (generator owned ≥ value), `flagSet` (a flag is set), `barsCompleted` (≥ value bars completed in a group), `recordsCumulative` (cumulative Records ≥ value), `compound` (all/any of nested Conditions).
modelNotes.conditionThresholds: A condition states its threshold as `value`, always — a condition compares against one. `amount` is a cost block's key, where the number is a price, not a threshold: `cost: { currency, amount }`. A condition object carries no other keys, so the importer reports any key it does not recognize (`amount` copied from the cost block beside a gate, or a plain misspelling) instead of dropping it and leaving the threshold at zero. A threshold must also be positive — the importer reports a non-positive one, boot validation reports it on existing assets, and the condition evaluates as unmet, so a broken gate blocks content rather than standing open.
modelNotes.flags: One flag registry drives every progressive reveal. A content-unlock upgrade's payload is `setFlag`; a reward's payload can also be `setFlag`; sections, currencies, bar groups, and any gated content reveal on a `flagSet` Condition. There is no separate `unlockSystem` code path — revealing a system = setting its flag.
modelNotes.bars: A 'Learn Covers' cover is a generic fillable BAR. A bar declares `fillCurrency` (a currency id) + `fillRequirement` + `reward`; the fill logic reads `fillCurrency` and never hardcodes covers. Rehearsal is an ordinary run-scoped currency; its per-press yield is a contribution on the jam producer and its passive per-sec trickle is a contribution on the `practice` producer (design §12 rule 13 — contributions live on contributors, never on the currency, and a contributor holds one kind of thing so its id is a promise a buff can rely on). Bars and their fill currency meet only through the `fillCurrency` id — mirrors how generators declare `produces`. A group's `fillMode` + `delivery` pair maps onto a concrete BarFillBehavior class at import (polymorphic, like Condition) — Ch1's pair is perBar + continuous. A new pair requires its behavior class to exist first, so authored data can never outrun implemented code.
modelNotes.addressables: Chapters, Sections, Producers, Generators, Upgrades, Events, Bars, BarGroups, Currencies, CurrencyGroups, Rewards, and StoryBeats are all loaded by Addressables label. Managers build their registries from whatever assets carry the label — no hardcoded lists, no direct scene/asset references.

currencies.cash: run-scoped; earned by tap + generators; spent on gear/upgrades
currencies.fans: run-scoped; performance meter; sets the album (demo) Records payout; loosely coupled to Cash by design
currencies.rehearsal: run-scoped; earned by a passive tick + taps; fills bars (Learn Covers) via each bar's fillCurrency
currencies.records: PERMANENT; each Record buffs global income; cumulative Records gate the capstone

chapter.name: Garage / Basement
chapter.theme: The band forms in a garage and plays its first backyard show.
chapter.note: The story beats moved to the `storyBeats` array below and the capstone threshold to `capstone.unlock` - both were second homes for something authored elsewhere. `capstoneRecordsGate` stated the same number as `capstone.unlock` while the Condition was the one nothing imported, and the beats were the only content kind with no definition of their own, which is why they could not be revealed or listed like anything else.

recordBuff.note: A multiplier declares which currencies it affects; generator production of anything it doesn't name is untouched. The Records buff is Ch1's only global multiplier and affects Cash.

constants.incomeFormulaNote: cashRate = sum(each cash `rate` contribution x its own multipliers) * (1 + 0.02 * records) * encoreBoost — the sum of the contributions times the product of the multipliers reaching `cash_rate`, which is the shape EVERY composed number in the game has (design doc rule 11). Catalog/Roadie multipliers are not present in Ch1. Cash's per-press yield is a separate number, `cash_yield`, summed from the jam line and stage_presence's; nothing multiplies a rate by seconds to reach it.

flags.reveals: Rehearsal currency + Learn Covers bar group
the capstone story beat; marks the chapter boundary
flags.note: Permanent-in-chapter (the default): a run-scoped completion flag would clear at the next release and re-open a finished chapter. ONE flag, not two - it is both 'this chapter is finished' and 'chapter 2 may open', and nothing in Ch1 can tell those apart. Set by the capstone completion operation itself, from `capstone.onComplete.completionFlag` - one declaration owns the fact, no payload carries a copy, and both the import lint and boot validation record the capstone as its setter.

flagsNote: The single reveal registry. A content-unlock upgrade (or a reward) sets a flag via a `setFlag` payload; anything that should appear when a system exists gates on `{ "type": "flagSet", "flag": <id> }`. Each flag's `scope` declares its latch's lifetime (absent = permanentInChapter, survives demos): a `run` flag clears at every album release, so everything gating on it goes dark together and re-arms when its run-scoped setter re-fires — the second-run flow re-walks the progression (band → fans → covers) instead of opening with everything taught. A run flag needs a run-scoped setter (linted at import, re-checked over the loaded assets at boot): with only permanent setters the rebuild re-asserts it in the same release. `setBy` is documentation only — the payload is the authoritative setter, and both the import lint and boot validation warn on a flag no content sets.

sections.name: The Garage Floor

modules.note: A module entry names the CONTRIBUTOR it fires - a definition sitting beside the module, never inside it, so other content can select it by id. Pressing the button fires the producers of the currencies that contributor holds yield lines for, and each producer pays its whole yield: stage_presence's +1 Cash is a contribution to cash's yield, so it is paid by the press without the button knowing it exists. Only an authored producer is fireable; a contributor is not a surface just because it holds a yield line. Modules that render a whole roster (the currency header above, generator/upgrade/bar lists) stay bare address strings.

sections.note: No visibleWhen: visible from chapter start. Module ids are Addressable keys resolved through a string→prefab registry loaded by label. A section shows exactly WHILE its visibleWhen holds — evaluated live, no latch of its own (progressive reveal, design doc §2). Persistence is authored in the STATE the condition reads: gate on a flag and the section inherits the flag's declared lifetime; gate on a monotonic value (earned totals) and it can never strobe; a threshold moment worth remembering is latched by a passive contentUnlock setting a flag (see browse_gear).

sections.name: The Band
sections.note: Appears with the Stage-0 goal; the practice_amp row unlocks at the same moment. Later sections gate on flags, e.g. { "type": "flagSet", "flag": "fans" }.

sections.name: The Gear
sections.note: The buff list. Shows while the run-scoped `gear` flag is set — latched by browse_gear the first time the run holds 250 Cash (stage_presence's own gate), so spending below 250 mid-run never hides a region you're using, and each demo re-hides it until the new run can afford gear again. Each row still appears and disappears on its own gate and purchase state.

sections.name: The Rehearsal Space
sections.note: The bars region: Learn Covers rows plus the Rehearsal readout. Gates on the covers flag (set by learn_covers at 25 Fans) — the same run-scoped flag that activates Rehearsal accrual and reveals the bar group, so the whole system appears as one moment, disappears at each demo, and re-opens as one moment when the run re-earns it.

sections.name: The Release
sections.note: The Cut a Demo (prestige) button, §5. Gates on the album flag (set by cut_demo at 50 Fans + 1 cover) like every other module — no bespoke reveal. The REGION stays through every demo after the first because the album flag's latch is permanent-in-chapter — while the button's pressability is the album block's `unlock` below, re-met each run.

sections.name: The Backyard
sections.note: The capstone offer (Play the Backyard Party), §5. Appears with the prestige loop — the first Record, the same moment garage_jam's availableWhen uses — and DELIBERATELY not at the capstone gate's own value: `capstone.unlock` is the SOLE home of the pacing knob, and a section threshold restating it would be a second copy able to drift. Region coarse, action precise, the exact the_release arrangement: the button's pressability is the capstone's authored unlock asked live, so the goal is visible (disarmed) through the mid-game climb and arms when the gate holds. Cumulative Records are monotonic and permanent, so the section can never strobe; after completion it stays, button dark, while the completion flag reveals the story beat.

generators.name: Practice Amp
generators.note: First automation. Unlocks the instant the Stage-0 goal (earn 100 Cash by tapping) is met.

generators.name: Drummer
generators.note: First bandmate. Buying the first one satisfies the play_for_crowd gate, which sets the `fans` flag. TWO lines, which is the shape the old produces/baseOutput pair could not hold: `kit_upgrade` doubles `drummer_cash` by name and leaves `drummer_fans` alone, while a buff naming `drummer` would reach both.

generatorsNote: A generator declares CONTRIBUTIONS (design doc §12 rule 13), each naming the currency it feeds, what quantity it is (`rate` per second, `yield` per firing) and its own id. Amounts are PER OWNED UNIT - the runtime scales by the count - so a bandmate's 0.02 fans/sec line IS the old `perBandmateOwnedBonus`, with no derived modifier reading a bool off every generator to add it. `isBandmate` is now the `bandmate` TAG (rule 10), which any buff can select and which nothing in code reads by name.

upgrades.name: Stage Presence
upgrades.note: +1 Cash per press. A flat bonus is a CONTRIBUTION to cash's yield (design doc rule 11), not an `add` effect granted against it: it sums with the jam line rather than composing over it, it has an id so a later buff can double this bonus specifically, and its lifetime is this upgrade's latch - a release clears the latch and the line goes with it, with nothing having to remember to withdraw it.

upgrades.name: Bigger Kit
upgrades.note: Names the LINE, not the generator. The drummer holds a cash line and a fans line, and 'Bigger Kit' doubles the cash one - `["drummer"]` would reach both, because a line offers its owner for a selector to match (design doc rule 11).

upgrades.name: Tight Set
upgrades.note: Gated on Fans, not Cash — demonstrates the gating web (§4). Same Condition shape as a Cash gate, just a different `currency` id, so no special-casing. The payload names cash's RATE by id — `cash_rate`, the number, not the currency — so it scales what accrues per second and never what a press pays. Naming `cash` would reach both of cash's numbers AND every line feeding them, applying once per line and again over their sum.

upgrades.name: Browse the Gear
upgrades.note: The passive threshold latch: the_gear section can't gate on the Cash balance directly (spending would strobe it), so the first time a run holds 250 Cash this sets the run-scoped `gear` flag and the section reads THAT. State remembers; the section just looks.

upgrades.name: Play for a Crowd
upgrades.note: Stage 2. Recruiting your first Drummer sets the `fans` flag — which reveals the Fans currency and meter. Run-scoped, like the flag it sets: each demo resets the band, so the fans meter goes dark and re-appears when the run's first Drummer is recruited — no fans display before a band exists.

upgrades.name: Learn Some Covers
upgrades.note: Stage 3. Sets the `covers` flag — reveals the Rehearsal currency and the Learn Covers bar group. Run-scoped, like the flag: rehearsal is meaningless without a band and an audience, so each demo the whole covers system (section, bars, accrual — everything gating on the flag) goes dark and re-opens as one moment when the run re-reaches 25 fans. This is what makes re-learning a cover a real leg of the release gate.

upgrades.name: Cut a Demo
upgrades.note: Stage 4. Sets the `album` flag — reveals the Release/Cut-a-Demo (prestige) button. This is the core teaching moment.

rewardsNote: The shared reward pool. Bars and event tiers reference these by id; each `type` is friendly vocabulary the importer maps onto a GameEffect - the same effect family an upgrade's `payload` builds - so a reward and a buff granting the same thing share one handler and one validator. A reward's `type` and an upgrade's `payload.effect` are two keys over ONE vocabulary: `setFlag` (with `flag: <id>`) and `multiplier`. A MODIFIER IS A MULTIPLIER (design doc rule 11): `add` used to live here and is gone, because a flat bonus is a `contributions` line on whatever pays it, not an effect granted against the number. `targets` says which numbers the multiplier reaches, and every term is a NAME - the id of something or the name of a tag, never a facet of something. ANY term matching is enough, so ["cash_rate", "fans_rate"] reaches both, exactly as it reads. Narrowing is done by naming the narrower thing: `cash_rate` is the id of cash's rate (derived from the currency, never authored), `drummer_cash` is one line of a generator that holds two, and a SET is named by tagging its members rather than by intersecting terms. AN EMPTY LIST reaches every number in scope, which is how a buff meaning double everything is authored; OMITTING the key is refused at import, because a forgotten key must not silently mean all of them.
rewardsScopeNote: A reward entry declares NO scope. The lifetime belongs to whatever applies it: a cover bar's reward lives as long as its bar group's `bars.scope`, an event tier's lives as long as the tier's own `scope`. That is one declaration per fact: a scope on the shared asset could disagree with the content paying it (a run-scoped bar granting a permanent multiplier would re-grant and compound every run), and it is what lets the same reward be a run payoff in one place and permanent in another.

currencies.note: The chapter's full local currency roster (design doc §12 rule 12): the economy context builds its pool from THIS list, never from every imported currency, so a currency belongs to exactly one economy. Chapter-placed groups only - a global currency (records) is held by the startup pool and naming it here is refused.

Rehearsal is a plain run-scoped currency: pure state — a balance, a group, formatting (design doc §12 rule 13). How it is earned lives on the `jam` and `practice` producers below, never here, and consumers (bars) reference it by id. `group` is the CurrencyGroupDefinition id the currency belongs to (reset behavior comes from the group's flags, like every currency).

producers.moduleNote: No `module` key: which module presents a producer is authored on the SECTION's module entry (`{ module, definition }`, see garage_floor above), and the runtime fires THAT producer's tap configs. The producer used to restate it here, validated and read by nothing, so a tap fired every tap producer in the chapter - two declarations of one relationship, able to disagree. A leftover `module` key is now refused at import. 'Nothing presents this producer' is derived instead: no section entry names it, which boot validation reports for a TAP producer (a surface nobody can press) and allows for a passive one like `band`.
producers.note: The Jam button's contributions (design doc §12 rule 13). ONLY press lines: a contributor's id is a promise about what it holds, so `jam` means 'what a press pays' and a buff reading '100x tap contributions' is the single term ["jam"]. The passive rehearsal trickle used to sit here and is its own contributor now (`practice`) - with it in this bundle, ["jam"] would have scaled a rate nobody presses for. `feeds` is the QUANTITY - a rate is per second, a yield is per firing - and there is NO trigger: what fires a producer is external and unnamed, so a button, an automation and a story beat are indistinguishable below the module. `trigger: tap` put a UI gesture in the economy's vocabulary and left the first demand-fired producer that is not a button press with nowhere to go. What accrues over an absence is structural (§9): a rate does, a yield cannot, because nothing fires a producer while the player is gone.

The passive Rehearsal trickle - 1/sec while the `covers` flag is set. A rate, so it accrues over an absence (§9) and nothing fires it; a peer of the `band` producer, and like it, presented by no module. It is a contributor of its own rather than a line on `jam` because a contributor's id is what buffs select: sharing `jam` would have made '100x tap contributions' silently multiply a passive rate too, and reaching both is something an author should have to say by naming both.

Fan accrual, as an ordinary contribution (design doc §12 rule 13) rather than a system of its own. No `module` key: nothing presents this producer, the player never touches it, and that is exactly the point — it is an ordinary rate line and accrues over an absence exactly as cash does (§9), with no exempt currency and no holder kind deciding it. This is the BASE fans rate; the per-bandmate bonus is now each bandmate's own `*_fans` line rather than a derived Add reading `isBandmate`, so fans/sec is (0.2 + 0.02×bandmates) × cover-bar rewards - the sum of the contributions times the multipliers reaching `fans_rate`, which is the one shape every composed number in the game has. The gate names the band directly — the base rate never checked for one, so before 5.7 the only thing tying accrual to having a band was which upgrade happened to set the `fans` flag.

groups.name: Learn Covers
groups.deliveryNote: How fill currency moves from the pool into the target. `continuous`: accrued Rehearsal streams into the group's active (player-selected) bar as it arrives; the pool only holds a balance when no bar is selected. The fillMode + delivery pair maps onto a BarFillBehavior class at import; future modes (tap a fixed chunk, dump the pool) are sibling classes with new vocabulary.
groups.fillModeNote: perBar / player-directed: each bar accrues its OWN progress by draining the shared Rehearsal pool; the player chooses which bar to pour Rehearsal into. Bars are independent (not cumulative thresholds on one counter). Totals: 120 + 300 + 600 = 1020 Rehearsal to finish all three.

bars.note: A bar is a generic fillable: it declares `fillCurrency` + `fillRequirement` + `reward`. The fill system reads `fillCurrency` and works for any currency — covers are just the Ch1 instance. Run-scoped: bars reset each demo but refill faster as the run gets stronger. cover_1 is on the critical path (its completion satisfies the barsCompleted leg of cut_demo). Bar rewards stack multiplicatively on fan rate.

fans.perBandmateNote: The per-bandmate bonus is no longer declared here. Each bandmate generator contributes its own 0.02/sec fans line (see `generators`), so band size raises the fan rate because a generator's contributions always scale with its owned count - not because a derived modifier reads an `isBandmate` bool off every generator and adds a lump. Two things went with it: a flat Add onto a number, which rule 11 says a bonus is not, and a chapter-level constant that the generators it described could not disagree with only because nothing let them differ.
fans.couplingNote: fanRate is intentionally NOT a function of Cash or Cash/sec — only band size, bar rewards, and time — so income alone cannot shortcut the demo payout (§11).

album.note: Releasing resets the run and awards Records. Reset is driven by currency group `resetsOnAlbumRelease` + upgrade/bar/flag `scope`, not a hardcoded name list. Flags and content unlocks split by their DECLARED scope, so `keeps` above is not a blanket rule: `album` (set by cut_demo) is permanent and The Release section stays visible across demos, while `fans`, `covers` and `gear` are run-scoped and clear together with their run-scoped setters (play_for_crowd, learn_covers, browse_gear) - which is what makes the second run re-walk band -> fans -> covers -> gear instead of opening with everything revealed. Sections carry no scope of their own: visibility is a live read of `visibleWhen`, so a section goes dark exactly when the facts behind it reset, and an earned-total gate resets because its currency's group does. Each Record = +2% permanent global income, so the next run is faster. `unlock` is the release OFFER's live gate: the button is pressable only while it holds, so it disarms at every release (fans and cover completions are run facts) and re-arms on the re-climb — the release OPERATION itself stays ungated, since the capstone implicitly cuts an album regardless.

events.name: Garage Jam Challenge
events.availableNote: Introduced in Stage 6, after the player has released at least one demo, so the prestige loop is understood first. Same `recordsCumulative` Condition type the capstone uses — one evaluator, different threshold.
events.baselineResetNote: On entry the chapter economy resets to a fixed baseline for the event's duration, so tiers scale independently of the player's Records.

tiers.scopeNote: How long a cleared tier stays cleared - the tier's OWN state, which slice 8 needs regardless of what the tier pays. permanentInChapter: you do not re-climb the Garage Jam ladder after every demo. What the reward granted projects from that clear and inherits its durability (design doc rule 11), which is why the reward declares no scope; a cover bar's fan-rate reward is run-scoped for the same reason in reverse, because bar completion is a run fact.

events.failNote: On a timed fail the event resets; the player can quit anytime. Cost is time only, never permanent progress.
events.tuningNote: Reward magnitude is the dial that sets how essential this event is (§6.1). As written it's a helpful-but-skippable tap booster; raise the reward to make it soft-required for reasonable pacing.

storyBeats.text: It starts in the garage. Just you, a beat-up amp, and a handful of songs you half-know. Time to make some noise.

The backyard's packed. You plug in, count off, and for three minutes the whole neighborhood is yours. Someone's already asking when the next one is — and a guy named Dave offers to haul your gear. You've got your first roadie.

storyBeatsNote: Story beats are ordinary content: a definition with an id and text, listed on the chapter, presented by a card module whose section entry names which beat it shows. They carry NO unlock and NO scope, because reveal is their SECTION's visibleWhen exactly as it is for the Jam button — beat_open in an always-visible section, beat_capstone in one gating on `chapter_2_unlocked`. Optional `readFlag` records that a beat was dismissed, for content that wants to gate on having read it; Ch1 authors none, so nothing records the read yet. Slice 10 builds the card prefab and places both in sections — a section pointing at a module address with no prefab fails boot validation, so the sections are authored there rather than here.

capstone.name: Play the Backyard Party
capstone.unlockNote: The SOLE authored source of the chapter gate, and the primary pacing knob. Imported through the same ConditionEvaluator every other gate uses; the old scalar `chapter.capstoneRecordsGate` is deleted rather than kept in step, because two homes for one threshold meant the authored Condition was the one being ignored.
capstone.onCompleteNote: Friendly keys split by category: grantRoadies imports as a one-shot ACTION (GrantCurrencyAction on the global `roadies` currency), executed exactly once by the completion operation - no release, load or reprojection can bank a second Roadie, because none of those paths execute actions. completionFlag is the capstone's own declaration; the operation latches it, and no setFlag effect is built from it, so a payload copy able to disagree with the declaration is not authorable. The Roadie allocation/replay UI stays locked until Chapter 2; there is no field for that here because a locked UI is the absence of a Chapter 2, not a fact to author.
capstone.storyBeatNote: No `fireStoryBeat` key: the capstone does not push a beat. `beat_capstone` below is revealed by its SECTION's visibleWhen gating on `chapter_2_unlocked`, which is the same pull every other module's reveal uses - setting the flag IS showing the beat.

balanceTargets.primaryPacingKnob: capstone.unlock.value — raise/lower before touching generator or fan curves
balanceTargets.primaryPacingKnobNote: This is a POINTER, not a second copy. It used to restate the threshold as `capstoneRecordsGate: 30` here as well, which is how a tuning number ends up with three homes and two of them stale.
balanceTargets.tuneAgainst: a player with full multiplier stack active (here just Encore up to 4x + records); confirm the chapter still takes meaningful play time
